module.title: Workplace listening: preparation, clarification and response
module.goal: Prepare to identify a message, preserve uncertainty and ask a precise clarification.
module.scope: Written preparation for listening with optional external British Council audio practice. No embedded or validated Irish-accent audio is supplied. Written checkpoints assess reading and response choices, not listening ability, pronunciation or acoustic fluency.

sections.title: 1. Set a listening purpose
paragraphs: The British Council listening collection offers preparation, recordings and comprehension tasks. For our original practice, decide what the workplace message needs to tell you: main point, important detail or next action. Transcribing every word can distract from the decision.

Before optional external audio, prepare a note frame: topic, action, owner, date and uncertain detail. Leave a field blank if you did not establish it. A guessed time must not become a confirmed appointment in your notes.
sections.supportPt: Defina o objetivo da escuta e mantenha incerto o que não conseguiu confirmar.

sections.title: 2. Notice repairs and conditions
paragraphs: Original written message for reading practice only: “The review is Thursday—sorry, Friday—at two, subject to room confirmation.” The corrected day is Friday; the room remains a condition. Do not treat abandoned Thursday as the final instruction.

The time two lacks an explicit a.m./p.m. or time-zone reference. Ask about it if material to the arrangement. This exercise cannot establish what the learner heard because the message is displayed as text.
sections.supportPt: Use a autocorreção final e preserve a condição. Texto exibido não mede compreensão auditiva.

sections.title: 3. Clarify the exact gap
paragraphs: Original response: “Friday at two, subject to the room being confirmed—is that 2 p.m. Dublin time?” It preserves known details and asks about a specific gap. Do not pretend certainty about the room or time reference.

If the whole message was missed, a broader repeat request is appropriate. Choose the repair that fits the gap. Requesting repetition is a communication strategy, not proof of poor pronunciation or a fixed proficiency level.
sections.supportPt: Peça esclarecimento proporcional à dúvida. Repetição é estratégia, não diagnóstico de nível.

sections.title: 4. Plan varied exposure honestly
paragraphs: Optional external practice: choose a recording from the linked collection, listen for the main point, then for selected details, and use the source transcript/tasks to review. This voluntary self-study does not create a saved Learning Hub score. No source audio is copied or played automatically.

Irish workplace exposure remains a separate requirement: select suitable permitted recordings, verify speakers/context and accessibility, and review comprehension fairly across valid varieties. This candidate does not label generic British Council material as Irish audio or infer accent tolerance from reading.
sections.supportPt: Prática externa é opcional. A exposição irlandesa precisa de gravações verificadas, não de texto simulando escuta.

terms.meaning: Central message needed for the task.
Specific item such as date or owner.
Speaker’s replacement of an earlier expression.
Requirement limiting a plan or claim.

terms.example: Reading is not an acoustic test.

visual.title: Workplace listening: preparation, clarification and response — decision map
visual.note: Original fictional exercise; not a live calculation or measured learner result.
visual.question: Which day should the response preserve?
visual.answer: Friday, while keeping the room condition and clarifying material time ambiguity.

caseStudy.title: Workplace listening: preparation, clarification and response — applied case
scenario: Original written message, not audio: “The review is Thursday—sorry, Friday—at two, subject to room confirmation.”
No other time reference or room confirmation supplied.
This exercise assesses interpretation of displayed text and response planning only.
caseStudy.task: Write a confirmation/clarification preserving the correction and condition.
hints: Clarify time without claiming the room is booked.
caseStudy.modelAnswer: Friday at two, subject to the room being confirmed—is that 2 p.m. Dublin time? The message does not establish that the room is booked. This is a response to displayed text, not evidence of listening or pronunciation.
reviewChecks: Specific clarification of material time uncertainty.
No acoustic score inferred from text.
caseStudy.transfer: With a permitted recording, identify what was heard before reviewing a transcript and keep the evidence type explicit.

checkpoint.prompt: The displayed message proves listening skill:
checkpoint.explanation: It is text, not audio evidence.
Generic external links do not establish Irish-accent coverage.

practiceExercises.question: Written message: “Send it on Monday—sorry, Tuesday.” Which day is final?
practiceExercises.explanation: This is reading/self-correction practice, not a listening measurement.

practiceExercises.question: You caught the date but missed the location. Ask a targeted question.
practiceExercises.answer: I have the date; could you confirm the location?

practiceExercises.question: You read a transcript and got every answer right. Can the app record strong listening or pronunciation?
practiceExercises.answer: No. This supports local written practice only; acoustic claims need appropriate audio evidence and validated assessment.
practiceExercises.explanation: Do not convert reading success into an acoustic result.

sources.label: British Council — B2 listening
sources.supports: External listening collection with preparation, audio and comprehension tasks. Its level label is not a learner assessment or Irish-accent verification.

professorGuide.opening: Ask what is confirmed, corrected and uncertain in the written message.
professorGuide.whenCorrect: Ask how clarification changes if only the location was missed, preserving the audio-evidence boundary.
professorGuide.whenUncertain: Ask which supplied fact is missing or unclear. Offer the first case hint, then invite another attempt.
professorGuide.whenMisconception: If they retain Thursday or confirm the room, point to the correction and condition, then invite a repair.
professorGuide.whenSelfCorrected: Use the corrected answer, not the abandoned phrase, as the current response. Ask one transfer question.
professorGuide.whenAskedForAnswer: Provide a concise explanation and one worked step; invite an optional fresh attempt without claiming independent mastery.
professorGuide.evidenceBoundary: Use only actual session evidence if this guide is separately integrated. Never consume local drafts or checkpoint results. Do not infer pronunciation/acoustic fluency from text, technical mastery from a phrase, or a CEFR level from one task.

assessmentBoundaries: Authored answer keys and guide branches are expectations, not model results or learner evidence.
